facts.raw_span: A 30-year-old gravida 2, para 1 woman
no significant medical history
no medication use
no history of trauma
bilateral ventriculomegaly with dilation of both frontal and occipital horns
irregular ventricular walls, multiple hyperechoic regions with indistinct margins within the ventricular lumens, and a roughened-appearing choroid plexus
normal middle cerebral artery perfusion
bilateral ventricular enlargement
areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles
TORCH panel returned within normal limits

platelet count, prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time, plasminogen levels, von Willebrand factor, factor V Leiden, protein S, protein C, and antiplatelet antibodies returned within normal limits
previous prenatal care had been irregular

concepts.why: Bilateral ventriculomegaly and ventricular enlargement with abnormal brain imaging suggest congenital hydrocephalus.
Irregular ventricular walls and multiple hyperechoic regions within the ventricles indicate fetal ventriculomegaly.
Normal TORCH panel and lab results make intrauterine infection less likely, but cannot be completely ruled out.
Normal coagulation studies and hematologic tests make fetal coagulopathy less likely, but cannot be completely ruled out.
Abnormal brain imaging and ventriculomegaly suggest congenital brain malformation.
Normal middle cerebral artery perfusion makes fetal cerebral vasculopathy less likely, but cannot be completely ruled out.
Irregular prenatal care increases the risk of undiagnosed infection.
Irregular prenatal care increases the risk of undiagnosed hematologic disorders.

rationales.F05: Bilateral ventriculomegaly is a strong indicator of Congenital Hydrocephalus and Fetal Ventriculomegaly.
rationales.F06: Irregular ventricular walls and multiple hyperechoic regions are indicative of Congenital Brain Malformation and Fetal Cerebral Vasculopathy.
rationales.F10: Normal TORCH panel results rule out Intrauterine Infection and Prenatal Infection Risk.
rationales.F11: Normal coagulation test results rule out Fetal Coagulopathy and Fetal Hematologic Disorder Risk.
